mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, which typically precedes positive equity returns as the economy expands and corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST rises by at least 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC for HOUST growth is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 0.05% signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS < 0.05), or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in labor force (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) above 0.5% and 0.3% MoM respectively signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive equity returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM and RSAFS > 0.3% MoM) fails to produce positive returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals sustained manufacturing output growth, which typically precedes positive equity returns as corporate profits expand before the cycle peaks.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPIAUCSL (inflation) over the past 3 months signals rising inflationary pressures that lead to central bank rate hikes, reducing real equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% MoM, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL growth is below -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE decline is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer spending (RSAFS) grows above 0.3% MoM and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.06%, the combination signals strong economic demand and accommodative monetary policy, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS > 0.3% MoM and FEDFUNDS < 0.06) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle economic expansions, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals the beginning of manufacturing recovery, which typically leads to positive equity returns as the economy transitions from recession to growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of early-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in early-cycle is below 0.03.
